question: to the Commission Anja Hazekamp (The Left) Subject:

An investigation by the Netherlands’ largest news organisation has revealed that, during transport from Ireland to the Netherlands, calves are not being given anything to drink for a period of around 24 hours. This is in breach of European regulations. Almost all of the calves tracked were unweaned animals that spent 50 to 80 hours in transit, some just two weeks old and still reliant on a milk diet1. Animal welfare organisations have been reporting for years that calves are being systematically deprived of milk for 30 to 48 hours during transport2. There have also been repeated reports of illegal transports, inadequate water systems, fabricated logbooks and mistreatment of calves345. 1.

Does the Commission agree that it is unjustifiable that, while the legislation is being revised, a process that has been ongoing for some years now, no measures are being taken to improve conditions for animals during transport?

Will you enter into discussions with the Dutch agriculture minister in the near future with a view to introducing the ban on the import of calves from Ireland to the Netherlands that has already been proposed?

Is the Commission prepared to launch infringement proceedings against Ireland due to its approval of illegal transports over many years and the failure of the Irish authorities to take action, in spite of previous requests and the Commission’s 2023 audit67?
answer: (English version) to the Commission Anja Hazekamp (The Left) (28 April 2026) Subject: Recent investigation into the transport of calves from Ireland to the Netherlands An investigation by the Netherlands’ largest news organisation has revealed that, during transport from Ireland to the Netherlands, calves are not being given anything to drink for a period of around 24 hours. This is in breach of European regulations. Almost all of the calves tracked were unweaned animals that spent 50 to 80 hours in transit, some just two weeks old and still reliant on a milk diet (1). Animal welfare organisations have been reporting for years that calves are being systematically deprived of milk for 30 to 48 hours during transport (2). There have also been repeated reports of illegal transports, inadequate water systems, fabricated logbooks and mistreatment of calves (3) (4) (5). 1. Does the Commission agree that it is unjustifiable that, while the legislation is being revised, a process that has been ongoing for some years now, no measures are being taken to improve conditions for animals during transport? 2. Will you enter into discussions with the Dutch agriculture minister in the near future with a view to introducing the ban on the import of calves from Ireland to the Netherlands that has already been proposed? 3. Is the Commission prepared to launch infringement proceedings against Ireland due to its approval of illegal transports over many years and the failure of the Irish authorities to take action, in spite of previous requests and the Commission’s 2023 audit (6) (7)? (23 June 2026) The report of the audit of Ireland carried out by the Commission in 2022 (1) confirmed that unweaned calves are not fed on rollon roll-off vessels as it is required by Regulation (EC) No 1/2005 (2) posing an infringement to the current rules. The Commission is closely monitoring efforts by the Irish authorities to achieve full compliance with Regulation (EC) No 1/2005. The information provided by the authorities shows the efforts being made to develop a system for automatic feeding of calves at ferry journeys. Member States do not have the possibility under EU law to ban the entry into their territory of animals from another Member State due to poor implementation of EU provisions under Regulation (EC) No 1/2005. The purpose of Regulation (EC) No 1/2005 is to harmonise EU rules on animal welfare during transport to ensure the smooth functioning of the internal market. It is the responsibility of each Member State to ensure a proper enforcement of these rules on their territory and cooperate with other Member States to ensure effective enforcement in case of cross-border situations. The Commission will continue working with the tools at its disposal, including the close monitoring of efforts by the Irish authorities, to ensure full enforcement of the provisions of Regulation (EC) No 1/2005.
